clue.text: Acts when ordered, for the most part an instrument

definitions.text: Acts when ordered, for the most part an instrument

indicators.note: once its letters are put in a new order the word acts is rearranged
only most of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a pawn is someone used as a tool by another

explanation.surface: A remark about a tool that mostly does what it is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ordered' rearranges ACTS to CATS; 'for the most part' cuts the final N from PAWN to give PAW. The whole clue is also the definition: a cat's-paw acts when ordered and is mostly an instrument, as the setter confirmed on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe used by someone else to do their dirty work is a mere tool who acts on command.

clue.text: Crash land-is mist circulating around old bomb site?

indicators.note: the letters go round and come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A plane crash-lands on a misty island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating around' rearranges CRASHLANDISMIST. Britain tested hydrogen bombs at this Pacific atoll in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiritimati, a Pacific atoll, was the site of British nuclear weapon tests in 1957-58.

clue.text: It's proven to be unlimited treasure

indicators.note: each word loses its limits, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A claim that a treasure has been shown to be boundless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips ITS to T and PROVEN to ROVE. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuables found, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Rear engineers stopping to gasp

indicators.note: the engineers plug the word for gasp, filling it like a stopper

parts.note: to pant is to gasp
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers at the back pausing for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping' puts RE inside PANT. 'Rear' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning bring up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to bring them up, as a mother or father does.

clue.text: You could watch a trailer with it

definitions.text: You could watch a trailer with it

parts.words: You could watch a trailer with it
parts.note: reads as a film preview seen on a screen, but the trailer is a vehicle towed behind, watched in the side mirror

explanation.walkthrough: A trailer looks like a cinema preview; here it is a towed vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver checks the vehicle behind using the mirror mounted on the side of the car.

clue.text: By first of the month, half of band left unit

parts.note: December is abbreviated to Dec
the Roman numeral I is one, the first

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for band survives, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: a belt is a band worn round the waist

explanation.surface: Someone counting the calendar while a band dwindles to half its size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps BE from BELT. 'By' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A decibel is a measure of loudness, one of the units of sound level.

clue.text: Difficult weed pulled up

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for weed is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to wee is to pee, so weed is peed

explanation.surface: A gardener finding a weed hard to pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns PEED round in a down entry. 'weed' looks like a garden plant, but it is the past tense of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep can mean hard to understand, as of a profound or abstruse problem.

clue.text: Nearly arrived at capital, needing small drink

indicators.note: most of the word for arrived is used, its last letter left off

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the capital is lacking a letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A traveller just reaching a capital city and wanting a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts CAME to CAM; 'needing' (lacking) takes S from PARIS. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is a bitter red Italian aperitif.

clue.text: One who influences Derby, say, after being given odds?

definitions.text: One who influences Derby, say, after being given odds?

parts.words: One who influences Derby, say, after being given odds?
parts.note: reads as a punter or tipster swaying a horse race, but Derby is also a cheese, and an influential person is a large one

explanation.walkthrough: Derby is a horse race and also a type of English cheese; an important person is called a large cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: An important, influential person is slang called a boss figure or top dog.

clue.text: Head stopping new school term, possibly to see tourist attraction

indicators.note: the headland plugs the rearranged letters, like a stopper
the letters might possibly be arranged otherwise

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in place names

explanation.surface: A head teacher interrupting the new school term to go sightseeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges N + SCHOOL + TERM to LOCHMONSTER; 'stopping' puts NESS inside. 'Head' looks like a teacher, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled creature of a Scottish lake draws visitors to the Highlands.

clue.text: Ring-road around English river

indicators.note: the letters are sent around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A ring road loops round a river somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges RINGROAD to RIOGRAND, then add E. The surface suggests an English river; the answer is on the US-Mexico border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande is a long North American watercourse forming part of the US-Mexico border.

clue.text: Exciting periodical I caught

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by the magazine they have picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exciting or wonderful can be called magic, as in 'it was magic'.

clue.text: Bone hard and swelling in the middle

parts.note: stern means hard or severe

indicators.note: only the middle of the word for swelling is kept, its outer letters gone

parts.note: a bump is a swelling

explanation.surface: A doctor describing a hard lump in the centre of a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' takes the first and last letters off BUMP, leaving UM.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: It's a pain to open new city

indicators.note: the a-and-pain pieces stand at the start, opening the word for new

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Complaining that a newly opened city is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to open' puts A + ACHE before N. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aachen is a German city near the Belgian and Dutch borders, Charlemagne's capital.

clue.text: Source of sprouts cooked among bones

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are altered, stirred into a new form

explanation.surface: A recipe in which some vegetables are cooked with bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges AMONGBONES. Bean sprouts are grown from these pulses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mung beans are the seeds sprouted to make bean sprouts.

clue.text: Starts to make wife and husband kiss soundly?

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following four words are taken

explanation.surface: An instruction for getting a married couple to embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition: the answer is the sound of an air kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise made with a theatrical air kiss is written as an exclamation of that sound.

clue.text: Dock five points following answer's obtuseness — on the contrary

indicators.note: the pieces for dock and five points come after the answer's letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
to dock is to cut
compass points: east, north, east, south, south

explanation.surface: A teacher deducting five marks from a dim pupil's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts CUT + ENESS after A. 'on the contrary' turns the definition to its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness of mind is the opposite of dullness or slowness to understand.

clue.text: Refuse to admit state's level of hanging?

indicators.note: the word for refuse takes another word inside it

parts.note: dross is waste matter, refuse
to opine is to state a view; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Someone declining to declare how far a picture droops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts OPINE inside DROSS. 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: How much something sags or dangles limply is the measure of its sagginess.

clue.text: Mum squeezing out about half the clues somewhere in England

indicators.note: the word for mum is pressed round another piece

parts.note: sh is the call for silence; to keep mum is to stay quiet
a crossword's clues are split into acrosses and downs

explanation.surface: Someone working on a crossword where half the clues have been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing' puts OUT inside SH, then add DOWNS; 'about' is a link. The South Downs are chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Downs are a range of chalk hills across Sussex and Hampshire, a place in southern England.

clue.text: Tough cowl on chimney

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a hood is a cowl
lum is a Scottish word for chimney

explanation.surface: A cowl fitted on top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough violent man, a thug or gangster.

clue.text: Vapour temperature splits weld

indicators.note: to split is to leave, so the temperature letter departs

parts.note: steam is water vapour

explanation.surface: Hot vapour bursting open a welded joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' means leaves: T goes from STEAM. It reads as cracks the weld.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces are joined, as in a welded joint.

clue.text: At last, hunter wears animal down

indicators.note: the animal has the letter on it, as if wearing it

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

indicators.note: the final letter of hunter is the piece used

explanation.surface: A hunter finally bringing down an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' gives R; 'wears' puts it inside MOOSE. 'down' looks like a verb, but it means unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means gloomy and sullen.

clue.text: Copper announced farewell

indicators.note: the letters for copper are spoken out loud

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer calls out goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the letters C U make the phrase. 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual goodbye promising another meeting is said as a farewell.

clue.text: Side of beef mostly rotten on top

indicators.note: the side of the word beef is its first letter
most of the word is kept, its last letter lost

parts.note: lousy means rotten, very bad

explanation.surface: A butcher complaining that a side of beef has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' takes the Y off LOUSY. 'top' is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouson is a short loose jacket gathered at the waist, an item worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Floats either normally or upside down

definitions.text: Floats either normally or upside down

parts.words: Floats either normally or upside down
parts.note: reads as a swimmer on front or back, but the written word itself looks the same when turned upside down

explanation.walkthrough: Turn the word upside down and the W becomes an M and the M a W, so it reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone afloat in water moves through it by stroking.

clue.text: First child's bond that's hard to break

indicators.note: the hard letter breaks away from the word for bond

parts.note: a chain is a bond
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A firstborn child's attachment that is difficult to break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' takes H from CHAIN. 'that's' and ''s' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cain was the elder son of Adam and Eve, the Bible's first-born.

clue.text: A kingdom that's short of space

indicators.note: the word for kingdom comes up short by its last letter

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom

explanation.surface: A small kingdom lacking room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's short' cuts the M from REALM.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal is an adjective meaning relating to an area or extent of surface.

clue.text: International body in a film one cuts?

indicators.note: the alliance sits within the other pieces

parts.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture
NATO is an international alliance

explanation.surface: A film about an international alliance, ending on the cutting-room floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NATO inside A + MIST. The question mark covers the definition: a dissector cuts bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who dissects bodies to study their structure makes cuts.

clue.text: Refuse to go out with him?

definitions.text: Refuse to go out with him?

parts.words: Refuse to go out with him?
parts.note: reads as a girl rejecting a date, but refuse is rubbish that leaves the house with the bin collector

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is the noun for rubbish, not the verb for saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: A bin collector takes household rubbish away each week.

clue.text: Poet writes in first half of The Archers, say

indicators.note: the word for writes goes inside the other piece
only the first three of the six letters are kept

parts.note: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap, an example of a serial
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A writer working on the opening half of a radio soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first half of' leaves SER of SERIAL; 'in' puts PENS inside it. The Archers is a British radio soap opera about farming folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene, an Elizabethan verse epic.
